About the Rijksmuseum

The Rijksmuseum is the national museum of the Netherlands, next to Museumplein in Amsterdam. The building was designed by Pierre Cuypers, the architect of Amsterdam Central Station, and opened in 1885, which makes it one of the oldest museums in Europe.

The collection covers Dutch cultural history from the Middle Ages to the 20th century. Around 8,000 objects are on display in the galleries, and the full collection held in storage is much larger.

The building is red brick, with walls decorated in patterns that reflect Dutch history and art. The glass-roofed atrium fills with natural light during the day, and the spiral staircase of the Cuypers Library is often named among the most beautiful libraries in the world.

1885
The present building opens to the public.
17th century
Masters of the Golden Age: Rembrandt, Vermeer, Frans Hals.
Today
Millions of visitors each year; Trip.com lists the museum in its 2026 Global 100 Best Things to Do.

Must-see

  • The Night Watch (1642)Rembrandt's most famous painting and the heart of the museum.
  • The MilkmaidJohannes Vermeer's celebrated painting of everyday life.
  • DelftwareThe distinctive blue-and-white Dutch pottery.
  • Cuypers LibraryA 19th-century library with a spiral staircase.
AddressMuseumstraat 1, 1071 XX Amsterdam, Netherlands
Opening hours9:00–17:00, according to Trip.com
Time neededRecommended: 3–5 hours
PhoneTicket inquiries: +31 20 674 7000

Best time to visit

  • Time of dayCome when the museum opens at 9:00, or after about 15:00. Midday is the busiest part of the day.
  • Day of the weekTuesdays and Wednesdays are usually the quietest. Avoid weekends: Saturday afternoon around 14:00 is typically the peak.
  • Time of yearApril, May and August are the busiest months, so visit outside them if you can.
  • BookingBuy a timed ticket online in advance. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

Two interesting facts

  • 1. The Night Watch was cut downWhen Rembrandt's painting moved to Amsterdam Town Hall in 1715, it had to fit between two doors, so strips of canvas were cut from three sides, mostly the left. The missing pieces were never kept.
  • 2. A public bike path runs through the buildingCyclists and pedestrians can pass straight through the museum along a passage at street level. It was part of the original commission, because the building was meant to link the old town with the new districts to the south.

Tip: buy tickets online in advance; they sell out quickly in summer and on rainy days. Opening hours and rules can change, so check the official website (rijksmuseum.nl).

Visa for the Netherlands

Citizens of Uzbekistan need a Schengen visa (type C) for a stay of up to 90 days in the Netherlands. The information comes from the Dutch government's official NetherlandsWorldwide website and from visa centre pages.

Important change. From 1 August 2026, applications for a Dutch Schengen visa in Tashkent are handled by the Polish embassy. Until 31 July they were submitted through VFS Global's Hungarian application centre.
Apply: e-Konsulat (Poland) Polish embassy Official Dutch page

Getting around Amsterdam

How to get from the airport to the city and to the Rijksmuseum. Prices are in euros and approximate for 2026 (sources differ slightly), converted to dollars and som.

To the museum: trams 2 and 12 go to the Rijksmuseum stop. From Schiphol Airport, bus 397 (Airport Express) drops you near the Museum Quarter and can save you a transfer.

Tip: paying with a contactless bank card (OVpay) costs roughly €1.50–3 per tram ride, with a daily cap so you never overpay. A GVB day ticket for children (ages 4–11) is €5.
